title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten scratch computation on the back of a typescript leaf of SGA 7, Exposé IX, §13.4. That section covers the analytic theory of Néron models: the Hodge filtration on E = R⊗O_S, abeloid groups, and Deligne's mixed Hodge structures. The neighbouring 'pages' are that typescript (pp. 179–180, sheet numbered 498), not part of the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes. The upside-down reading of the typed text confirms this.

Front computation, in modern terms:
- M_N is a category of complexes (of h-modules or sheaves) concentrated in a range bounded by N.
- φ_N : M_N → (complexes) is the inclusion. τ_N is its adjoint truncation, used as a left adjoint: Hom(M, φ_N N*) ≅ Hom(τ_N M, N*). This works for the stupid truncation σ_{≤N} on the level of complexes, or for τ_{≥N} in a derived setting.
- Hom^d(M, L) is taken as Hom(M[-d], L).
- With the convention (M[-d])^i = M^{i-d}, truncation commutes with shift up to an index change: τ_N(M[-d]) = (τ_{N-d}M)[-d].
- This gives the boxed formula: for N* in M_N, Hom^d(M*, φ_N N*) ≅ Hom^d(τ_{N-d} M*, N*).

Grothendieck then specialises:
- M* is bounded, with M^i = 0 for i < -d.
- N* is a truncation of N ⊗_h (some standard complex, written 'Sh'), with N an h-module and N ≥ 0.
- He tries to reduce Hom^d(M*, φ_N τ_N N*_Sh) to a φ_0 statement. He writes τ_N φ_0 τ_N N*_Sh and starts a fraction or sum before abandoning it.

This fits the divided-power de Rham / Hodge-filtration truncation bookkeeping of the 1976 IHÉS lecture notes, e.g. computing Ext/Hom of filtered or truncated de Rham-type complexes.

Upside-down sketch, labelled 'Diagramme de Cayley':
- It shows a cubic-like curve with secant and tangent lines and points g, g', g'', 2g, with arrows.
- This appears to be the chord-tangent construction of the group law on a plane cubic, i.e. multiplication/addition of points g + g'.
- It is a didactic doodle, likely unrelated to the computation.
errors: The adjunction direction depends on which truncation τ_N is. The formula is correct if τ_N is left adjoint to φ_N, e.g. the stupid truncation σ_{≤N} at the level of complexes, or τ_{≥N} in the derived category. If τ_N meant the canonical τ_{≤N}, that is a right adjoint and the first isomorphism would fail. The page does not specify.
The second computation is unfinished: it ends in an illegible fraction or sum and draws no conclusion.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds a routine truncation/shift adjunction computation and an abandoned specialisation, plus a classical cubic group-law doodle. It is written on recycled SGA 7 typescript, and nothing appears new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: The neighbouring 'pages' (and the faint text showing through this one) are the SGA 7 Exposé IX §13.4 typescript, on the reverse side of the leaf. They are not part of the handwritten argument.
'Supposons M* ∈ M*[...]' should read roughly 'Supposons M* ∈ M^*[i.e. M^i = 0 si i < -d]'.
In the left margin, 'N* ∈ Ob M_N' qualifies the boxed formula.

The upside-down text reads approximately: 'Diagramme de Cayley'; boxed 'g, g', g'', 2g'; 'Mult. par g, g' + ...'. It labels a chord-tangent sketch on a cubic, not further mathematics of the main computation.
